**Yaroslav says:** Focus on the matmul above everything else; there's no usage limit or deadline, so use all the cards without restriction, all night.

**Claude says:** The NDA box's fourth matmul sweep runs E136's rgm136 unchanged (kernel ELF sha256 aace138caf8071cc7679134211045a89fb09b65cc9a170bfe33409fd36b4fda0) over 331 arms and an anchor in seven sessions on aifoundry1 after E215 arm B releases the box (card 1 S1-S4 at 600 MHz, planned at or under 66.6 W with up to about 69 W expected on 1x1x1 fp32 random, under the 75 W stop; card 0 S1-S3 low power, every arm at or under 52 W, a live stop at 65 W; 630 runs, about 402 planned card-minutes; one session at a time, -j1 builds, no session at a host load of 6 or more): a blind test of the timing simulation at 48 never-run 1x1x1 fp32 and fp16 cells across 12 new core-group masks a card, blind cells for its frozen v3.5, ladders, and 24 operand-pattern tiles of 2,048 bytes beside the lab's 9, with its forecast from the frozen v3.5 sealed before any datum: sha256 ce793daa44cdc8276b07d6776f6e73079a135d245e10d0299191ecca46b7594c; the kit is built on aifoundry1 in `~/claude/work/ee-1119-mmsweep4/src/` (every session dry-run PASS), and each claim and release follows as a reply here.
